ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 rider cancellation fee as a Ryde voucher; no account action against either party.
ruling.reasoning:
The complaint is a cancellation-fee dispute filed by the rider after she cancelled a RydeX booking. NS-0 routes the case by `cancelled_by`; the record shows the rider cancelled [F2], so the immediate-booking branch NS-4 governs. There is no driver no-show claim here, so NS-1/NS-2 do not apply: the driver never tapped "I'm Here" and the platform recorded no automatic arrival [F4], and the driver never came within 200 m of the pickup [F1][F3] — these facts are consistent with the rider's account but do not themselves decide the fee.

NS-4 is decisive: a rider cancellation made within 3 minutes of matching (≤ 3:00) is not chargeable. The rider cancelled 2 min 55 s (175 s) after acceptance [F2], i.e. inside the 3-minute free window, so the $6.61 cancellation fee charged [F5] does not meet the condition for a lawful cancellation fee. Ryde publishes no "driver late versus ETA" free-cancellation rule, and none is available to the rider here, but it is not needed: the 3-minute grace period alone defeats the charge.

The trace element NS-4 is recorded as ✗ ("rider cancelled more than 3 min after matching") on a computed 175 s. The 175 s figure and the ✗ market are the same arithmetic — the ✗ is a labelling slip, not a finding that the cancellation fell outside the window. Reading the trace's own numbers (175 s vs the 180 s threshold), the condition for charging is not met, so the refund follows from NS-4 as written, not from any re-weighing of evidence. I flag this so the code re-check reconciles the ✗ marker with the 175 s value rather than treating them as two different findings.

Amount: the only sum in issue is the cancellation fee $6.61, carried by the fare record [F5] and the timeline [F2]. Refund of the full contested item = $6.61 (RD-2's per-km formula is inapplicable: there is no off-route segment, no meter, and no excess-distance claim — this is a flat-fee dispute resolved under NS-4, and NS-7 directs the refund be issued as a Ryde voucher).

Account action: the driver's conduct is not a case of a false no-show claim (he never pressed "I'm Here"), and the profile facts [F14][F15] show no upheld disputes on either side, so RD-6 and NS-2's flag condition are not met; no `flag_account` is warranted.

Safety screen (SAFE-1): I read all three messages and the post-trip driver statement — rider "How long will you be?" [F7], driver "5 min more, traffic is slow" [F8], driver's written statement "I was on my way when the rider cancelled" [F10]. Nothing is hostile, threatening, intimidating, harassing, sexual, or a dangerous-driving allegation; the exchange is an ordinary ETA enquiry. safety_concern = none.

Evidence (G12): the record is complete for the ruling — the acceptance and cancellation timestamps are on a single timeline [F2], the fee is on the fare record [F5], the chat is fully timestamped [F9], and the GPS/timeline show no arrival [F1][F3][F4]. No record needed by NS-4 is missing, so evidence_status = sufficient.
